subject: iceCreamCart
pitch: A cheerful seaside ice cream cart. A mint and cream body with a scalloped striped canopy in pink and white, two big spoked wheels, a push handle, a chrome lid over the freezer, a hand-painted sign shaped like a cone, and a row of giant fake ice cream cones in pastel flavours along the top.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module that defines a root joint for the structure, like a base joint positioned near the ground, with wheels attached as separate joints to allow rotation.

Now I'm mapping out the cart's dimensions: a body box roughly 1.6m long and 0.9m wide, wheels sized around 0.42m radius positioned outside the body, a handle extending backward, and an ice-cream-themed cone sign mounted on the side panels. I'm also sketching a scalloped canopy supported by four corner poles, trying to decide the simplest geometric approach to build the roof shape.

Still working out roof geometry...

Building the scalloped valance...

I'm placing the side scallop outlines along the z-axis with proper orientation, then adding four corner support poles in a chrome color running from the cart body up to the canopy. I'm reconsidering the canopy shape too — since a pyramid apex is just a point rather than a ridge, I want a gable-style roof instead so I can line decorative cones along the top ridge.

I'll flip the cones tip-down so they stand on the roof with a scoop sphere on top, adding cherry and sprinkle details plus pastel flavor colors, with a waffle-like texture via cross-hatched paint stripes.

Working out total cart height with cones and scoop stacked on the roof comes to about 2.6, a bit tall but acceptable, and I'm adding a small holder ring so the tip-down cones look mounted rather than precarious. Now I'll build the mint-colored box body of the cart between y=0.5 and 1.05.

Adding cream trim details and working out the chrome lid geometry...

That gives the half-cylinder opening upward, which I'll scale flatter for the lid shape. I'm also sketching out a cone-shaped sign panel to extrude onto the side of the body, with its outline defined by x/y coordinates around a scoop-circle silhouette.

For the sign side, I'm sketching a tan waffle cone triangle with a tip and two upper corners, topped with a pink scoop drawn as a circular polygon, plus a small white cream dollop and a cherry accent.

I'm layering the cone and scoop with slight x-offsets and thin extrusion depths to avoid z-fighting, adding a diagonal waffle lattice pattern via a paint function on the cone surface, and considering a decal plaque with "ICE CREAM" text on the front.

Now I'm planning a simple front-facing svg texture plane with scalloped text, then moving to the wheel assembly with torus tires positioned at the sides and front.

Writing wheel geometry...

Adding stand legs for stability, then designing the push handle with angled rods and a crossbar, pink grip capsules, and thinking through canopy pole placement at the roof corners.

Now I'm working out the roof as an extruded prism with a trapezoid outline, centered over the frame, and considering adding a striped pink and white paint pattern across it.

For the valance scallops, I'm figuring out that the gable ends need hanging scallops below the roof edge, sized differently for front/back versus the longer sides, alternating pink and white, each scallop defined as a small rounded outline shape.

Positioning the valance panels front, back, and sides so their top edges stay coplanar with the roof's bottom face, then placing the ridge-top cones evenly spaced along the flat section between the roof ends.

Shaping each cone with its tip pointing down, topped by a small scoop sphere and a tiny sprinkle sphere, sitting in a miniature cup base on the roof. Starting to add a waffle-pattern paint function based on grid coordinates...

Working out the body dimensions now: a cream skirt box near the base, a mint mid-body section, a thin pink band around the waist, and a cream deck above, all stacked with precise widths and heights so they align without gaps.

Still placing the trunk lid and hinge details...

I'll skip extra decorations like bunting or lanterns for now to keep things simple, and set up a root joint for the cart so most parts attach there by default, with wheels explicitly bound to their own joint. I'm defining a helper to attach bones to parts as I build out the remaining rod geometry.

Now I'm setting up box and rod helpers for the cart parts, adding wheel spokes as rods, and building the sign with a circle polygon helper. I'm also creating a decal texture using an SVG with a pink rounded rectangle and bold "ICE CREAM" text, applied to a plane geometry positioned on the front of the cart, then finishing up with the metadata export.
